title: Minimal polynomials and nilpotent Jordan structure
terms: annihilating polynomial; minimal polynomial; Jordan block; Jordan normal form; nilpo- tency index.

exposition.text:
The minimal polynomial m is the monic polynomial of least degree satisfying m (A) = 0.
A A
It divides every annihilating polynomial, including the characteristic polynomial. Over a field
where it splits, A is diagonalizable exactly when m has no repeated roots. Over C, Jordan
A
normal form expresses A as a direct sum of blocks λI + N, where N has ones above the diagonal
and is nilpotent.
The exponent of t − λ in m is the size of the largest block for λ; its exponent in the characteris-

tic polynomial is the total size of those blocks. For a nilpotent matrix, dim ker A − dim ker A
counts blocks of size at least k. These increments are nonincreasing and their sum eventually
reaches the whole dimension.
A polynomial p with p(A) = 0 is an annihilating polynomial. A nilpotent matrix satisfies
r
A = 0 for some positive integer; its nilpotency index is the least such integer, and is the size
of its largest Jordan block. Repeated-root tests must be performed in the actual scalar field,
whose characteristic can change a polynomial's factorization.

1) (t + 2). What is the largest possible dimension of its 1-eigenspace?
(A) 1 (B) 2 (C) 3 (D) 4 (E) 5

solution.text:
The 1-blocks have total size 4, with largest size exactly 2. To maximize their number,
choose sizes 2, 1, 1, giving three independent 1-eigenvectors. Four size-1 blocks would
contradict the square factor in the minimal polynomial. The −2 blocks do not affect this
eigenspace.

The polynomial identity gives A = A , hence A = A , so A is idempotent. The matrix
